answer: Picture an agent economy as a meadow where any newcomer may wander in, but grazing rights require a bond. Each new identity locks a deposit that vests only after months of honest, peer-attested work, and is slashed if its votes correlate suspiciously with other accounts. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand agents must lock a thousand deposits and wait out every vesting clock, turning a cheap stroll into a costly climb up a mesa.
